title: Universal cyclotomic Hecke ordered monomials form a basis
statement: For R=Z[z^(±1),U_1^(±1),...,U_ℓ^(±1)], ℓ>=1, the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation at first polynomial ∏_a(X_1−U_a) is free with indexed R-basis X^a T_w, 0<=a_r<ℓ,w∈S_n. This basis specializes to every commutative R-algebra. Rankzero is R with singleton empty word. The separate levelzero positive-rank quotient is zero with empty family.

# Explicit universal PBW binding for the local trace and Schur constructions

Same pending first native24 repair. This is necessary prerequisite construction, not a native registration or acceptance claim. Let R=Z[z^{±1},U_1^{±1},...,U_ell^{±1}], ell>=1, and let H_n be the actual nondegenerate cyclotomic presentation with first-variable polynomial product(X_1-U_a). The bounded ordered family B={X^a T_w:0<=a_i<ell,w in S_n} is an R-basis, conditional only on the independently constructed early field BK-sector isomorphism, the existing cyclotomic KLR ordinary Hom norm dimension, and elementary finite-field existence/root bounds.

Spanning is already the exact universal-ring calculation in basis-proof-construction/helper-registration-drafts.json, first helper. Bernstein product identities transport the first polynomial to a zero relation with leading z^(r-1)X_r^ell, all remainders having r-exponent<ell and no variable above r. Reverse lexicographic induction terminates; its leading coefficients are units of R. Inverse variables are polynomials using the first polynomial's unit constant term and invertible finite Hecke generators. These calculations use no field division and therefore hold over R.

For independence suppose sum_b f_b b=0 with a nonzero Laurent coefficient f. After multiplying by a Laurent monomial, choose a prime p at which a nonzero integer coefficient of f survives. View f as a polynomial in U's with coefficient polynomials in z. Choose a nonzero such coefficient g(z). In arbitrarily large finite fields F_(p^d), the number of primitive nonzero elements is phi(p^d-1), which tends to infinity. For explicit bounds phi(N)>=sqrt(N/2): factor over prime powers; each factor phi(r^a)^2/r^a=r^(a-2)(r-1)^2>=1 except r=2,a=1, where it is 1/2. Thus choose d with phi(p^d-1)>deg g, p^d-1 larger than each U-degree, and p^d-1>=2. Some primitive z avoids the roots of g. Repeated one-variable root bounds on the full nonzero-coordinate grid supply U_a!=0 with f(z,U)!=0. Each U_a is a power z^(c_a).

This specialization is exactly an allowed finite cyclic type-A field parameter: z has order e=p^d-1>=2, and the cyclotomic charges c_a lie in Z/eZ. The early explicit BK maps identify the direct sum of Hecke central sectors with the standard homogeneous cyclic KLR algebra. The ordinary first Ind/Res adjunction, projective preservation and v=1 mixed commutator give the independent integer total dimension ell^n n! by the regular-Hom norm helper. Bounded spanning provides exactly that many ordered words, so the specialized B is a field basis. Consequently its specialized relation forces every f_b(z,U)=0, contradicting the chosen f. There was no inference of integral freeness from generic rank, no assumed flatness and no use of Schur or primitive-block classification.

It follows that the displayed spanning family is free over R. Formation of the presented algebra commutes with arbitrary base change: generators and relations define a quotient of a free algebra and its specialized ideal is precisely the specialized relation ideal. Hence the R-basis specializes to a basis over every commutative R-algebra, including the LM deformation DVR with z=q_H t and U_a=Q_a t^(na). Universal Murphy independence can use the identical density argument after its independent universal spanning calculation.

Dependency order is essential: primitive-free early spectral/projector sectors and explicit field BK maps precede the field norm and late field basis; this universal PBW helper follows those. It then feeds the local canonical trace and perfect Gram proof, Murphy/semistandard/Schur constructions and Jantzen. The original bundled ResidueDefinition primitive clause(iv), late original Hecke basis wrapper, and Schur block result must never feed the early BK construction.

For n=0 the singleton empty word gives H_0=R directly. For ell=0,n>0 the quotient is zero and the empty basis is immediate; the universal parameter ring above and trace tau(1)=1 are not invoked in that zero case.

title: The universal cyclotomic Hecke canonical trace is perfect and symmetric
statement: For the preceding universal cyclotomic presentation, extract coefficient of the zero-dot identity-permutation PBW word to define τ. Then τ(ab)=τ(ba) and (a,b)↦τ(ab) is a perfect R-bilinear associative pairing. Both properties hold after every commutative unit-parameter base change, including the LM DVR. Rankzero is R with τ(1)=1_R. For the separate levelzero positive-rank zero algebra the zero pairing is perfect; no nonzero trace1 assertion is made.

# Complete local canonical-trace cyclicity construction

Same author and same pending native24 repair 1/max2. Construction only; parent retains supplier acceptance, original consumer ownership, integration, and root gate authority.

## Full local proof

Write q=q_H and f(t)=t^ℓ+c_(ℓ−1)t^(ℓ−1)+…+c_0=∏_(a=1)^ℓ(t−Q_a), with ℓ≥1. Assume the independently proved universal ordered PBW basis; no trace assertion is part of this input. For n≥1 put H_n for the rank-n cyclotomic algebra, H_0=R. PBW identifies H_(n−1) with the subalgebra on X_1,…,X_(n−1),T_1,…,T_(n−2): its bounded words are a subset of the H_n basis. Let v_n=1 and v_k=s_(n−1)…s_k for 1≤k<n. The finite Hecke left-coset decomposition w=u v_k with u∈S_(n−1) is length additive. Since X_n commutes with all generators of H_(n−1), PBW gives the left H_(n−1)-basis {X_n^a T_(v_k):0≤a<ℓ,1≤k≤n}. Define the left-linear projection E_n:H_n→H_(n−1) by E_n(X_n^aT_(v_k))=1 for a=0,k=n and zero otherwise. Its PBW coefficient interpretation gives τ_n=τ_(n−1)∘E_n, where τ_0 is the identity R→R.

For n>1 prove E_n(hX_1)=E_n(h)X_1 on this left basis. If k=n, then X_n commutes with X_1, giving the claim. If k>1 but k<n, each factor of T_(v_k) has index at least two and commutes with X_1, giving the claim. Only k=1 remains. Write V=T_(n−1)…T_1 and U=(T_(n−1)−q+1)…(T_1−q+1). The mixed relation T_jX_j=X_(j+1)(T_j−q+1) gives VX_1=X_nU. Thus, if 0≤a<ℓ−1, X_n^aVX_1=X_n^(a+1)U has positive bounded X_n-degree. Expansion of U in finite Hecke words and their left-coset decomposition shows E_n of this expression is zero.

At a=ℓ−1 the same expression is X_n^ℓU, so a separate cyclotomic argument is necessary. For every m≥1, Bernstein straightening gives
T_jX_j^m=X_(j+1)^m(T_j−q+1)−(q−1)Σ_(b=1)^(m−1)X_j^b X_(j+1)^(m−b).
Applying this successively along V proves VX_1^m=X_n^m U+J_m, where J_m is a linear combination of polynomial–finite-Hecke terms of total dot degree m, each with X_n-degree between 1 and m−1 and no variable above n. Here J_1=0. To see the bound inductively, at each step the active variable has a positive exponent c≤m. The leading branch transfers c to the next variable; every correction transfers a positive exponent strictly below c. Earlier variables commute with the next crossing. Once a correction has occurred, the final X_n-exponent remains below m; no branch transfers exponent zero. This also proves that the leading branch is exactly X_n^mU. For m≤ℓ, every lower exponent in J_m is individually below ℓ because X_n-degree is positive and total degree is at most ℓ. Hence these are already bounded polynomials, and finite Hecke left-coset straightening preserves positive bounded X_n-degree. Therefore E_n(J_m)=0 for m≤ℓ. Also E_n(X_n^mU)=0 for 1≤m<ℓ, and E_n(V)=0 because v_1 is a nonidentity left coset.

Now the actual first-dot relation, multiplied by V, is 0=Vf(X_1)=X_n^ℓU+J_ℓ+Σ_(m=1)^(ℓ−1)c_m(X_n^mU+J_m)+c_0V. Applying E_n gives E_n(X_n^ℓU)=0. This completes the missing a=ℓ−1 case, including ℓ=1 (then every J_m and the positive lower-power sum is empty). Thus E_n(hX_1)=E_n(h)X_1 for all h. By left linearity E_n(X_1h)=X_1E_n(h), and induction using τ_n=τ_(n−1)E_n proves τ_n(X_1h)=τ_n(hX_1). The base n=1 is the commutative algebra R[X_1]/f(X_1); n=0 is R. This uses neither individual relations f(X_r)=0 nor assumed trace invariance.

It remains to check finite generators T_j directly on every PBW element pT_w with p=X^a bounded. Bernstein gives T_jp=(s_jp)T_j+(1−q)X_(j+1)(p−s_jp)/(X_j−X_(j+1)). For p=X_j^aX_(j+1)^b times the other variables, the correction monomials have the same total dot degree, and both displayed-variable exponents are at most max(a,b)<ℓ: when a>b the correction exponents are (a−1−k,b+1+k),0≤k<a−b, and when a<b they are (a+k,b−k),0≤k<b−a, with the corresponding sign. Thus, when the exponent profile is positive, every term on either side of τ(T_jpT_w)=τ(pT_wT_j) has a positive bounded profile and value zero; no cyclotomic reduction occurs. When p=1, the finite Hecke multiplication formula gives coefficient of 1 in T_jT_w or T_wT_j equal to q if w=s_j, and zero otherwise. This proves finite-generator cyclicity without using the sought trace.

Finally X_1 and T_1,…,T_(n−1) generate H_n as an R-algebra. Indeed c_0=(−1)^ℓ∏Q_a is a unit, so f(X_1)=0 makes X_1^(−1) a polynomial in X_1; each T_j^(−1)=q^(−1)(T_j−q+1), and X_r=q^(1−r)T_(r−1)…T_1X_1T_1…T_(r−1), with inverses expressed likewise. Move the generators of a word one at a time around τ, using the identities proved above, to obtain τ(ab)=τ(ba) for every pair of words and hence all a,b by R-bilinearity. No generic-faithfulness, reduced-basis trace, or imported Bremke–Malle cyclicity is assumed.

# Universal cyclotomic Hecke symmetrizing trace: actual local route

SAME native24 pending first repair construction; no native/canonical/readiness/gate mutation. This closes the universal trace input once the named universal PBW and the local cyclicity lemma bind. It does not close Q-S1 or the Schur Jantzen weight Gram identity. The Hecke parameter is q_H throughout, unrelated to grading v.

Let R=Z[q_H^(±1),Q_1^(±1),...,Q_ell^(±1)], ell≥1, and H_n be the nondegenerate monic cyclotomic affine-Hecke quotient. Assume the independently constructed universal PBW basis B={X_1^a_1...X_n^a_n T_w:0≤a_i<ell,w∈S_n}. Define τ(B)=1 exactly at all a_i=0,w=1 and zero elsewhere. The complete local tower proof in basis-proof-construction/canonical-trace-cyclicity-local-proof.md supplies τ(ab)=τ(ba): its E_n projection, top monic-degree case and finite Bernstein calculation were read and checked. No Bremke–Malle trace statement is imported. Prove perfectness as follows.

1. Set J_1=1,J_i=q_H^(-1)T_(i-1)J_(i-1)T_(i-1) in the finite Hecke subalgebra. These are units, since all T_i and q_H are units. Define δ(0)=0,δ(c)=−1 for c>0 and the second family
C={T_v J_1^δ(c_1)...J_n^δ(c_n) X_1^c_1...X_n^c_n:0≤c_i<ell,v∈S_n}.
The standard anti-involution fixing the presentation generators fixes each X_i. Thus B*= {T_v X^c} is a basis. At each fixed profilec, multiplying the finite Hecke factor by the unit J_1^δ(c_1)...J_n^δ(c_n) is an invertible R-linear change of the finite Hecke basis. Hence C is an R-basis. This uses actual universal PBW, not flatness or generic semisimplicity.

2. Let V_j be the span of X_1^a_1...X_j^a_j T_w,0≤a_i<ell,w∈S_n. It is stable under left multiplication by lower-rank polynomial generators and right multiplication by finite-Hecke elements: the lower-rank algebra embeds by PBW and its monic reductions stay in that rank. For h∈V_j and 0<s<ell, τ(X_(j+1)^s h)=0 by the defining coefficient rule. This is immediate bounded ordered PBW, not a per-dot cyclotomic relation.

3. The exact Bernstein identity (obtained by its product rule) is, for k≥m,
X_i^k X_(i-1)^m T_(i-1)=T_(i-1)X_i^m X_(i-1)^k+(q_H−1)Σ_(c=m+1)^k X_i^c X_(i-1)^(k+m−c),
with the reversed version obtained by the presentation anti-involution. It gives the telescoping identity
X_i^k=q_H^(-1)T_(i-1)X_(i-1)^kT_(i-1)+q_H^(-1)(q_H−1)Σ_(c=1)^(k−1) X_i^c X_(i-1)^(k−c)T_(i-1).
For 1≤i≤j+1 and 1≤k≤ell it follows that
τ(X_(j+1)^k h)=q_H^(i-j-1)τ(T_j...T_i X_i^k T_i...T_j h), h∈V_j.
Here is the source-adapted downward induction, with its boundedness premise explicit. The base i=j+1 is identity. Substitute the preceding telescoping formula in the induction term. The leading summand is the next i−1 term. In every correction0<c<k, move one adjacent X through the inverse string T_i^(-1)...T_j^(-1), using T_a^(-1)=q_H^(-1)(T_a+1−q_H) and the displayed Bernstein rule. It becomes a sum of finite-Hecke factors followed by dot monomials, with X_(j+1)-exponent b≤max(c−1,k−c−1)≤k−2. The original moved dot supplies one further X_(j+1), so the resulting exponent is in1,...,k−1<ell. All other factors belong to V_j after lower-rank monic reduction. Cyclicity rotates only the explicit finite-Hecke factors, and the coefficient-zero rule in2 kills each correction. Thus the downward induction holds. This reproduces the actual complete calculation of Malle–Mathas Lemma3.7; its trace premise is now our local tower lemma. No foreign center/semisimplicity claim is used.

4. Put α=(−1)^(ell+1)Q_1...Q_ell. Take i=1,k=ell in3 and reduce the FIRST variable X_1^ell with its actual polynomial ∏(X_1−Q_a)=0. The terms of degrees1,...,ell−1 vanish by3 and2; the constant coefficient is (−1)^ell productQ_a and moves to the other side with a minus. Therefore
τ(X_(j+1)^ell h)=α τ(h J_(j+1)).
For j=0 the same equation is the direct first-variable polynomial calculation with J_1=1. The acquired author-preprint Proposition3.8 prints the opposite sign. Our coefficient is forced by the monic relation, confirmed at ell2,n2, and is a UNIT either way. We do not silently import the literal erroneous sign.

5. Let G_j be the pairing matrix between B,C restricted to profiles whose entries abovej are zero, with all finite permutations still included. Its size N_j=ell^j n!. Order new last profiles by b_(j+1)=0,1,...,ell−1 and c_(j+1)=0,ell−1,ell−2,...,1. Cyclicity rotates the rightmost dot monomial to the front, combining its exponents with the left dot monomial. If both new exponents are0, the block is G_j. If0<b+c<ell, it is zero by2. If b+c=ell, formula4 applies; the right factor J_(j+1)^(-1) occurs because c>0, and cancels the J_(j+1) in4. The block is αG_j. Terms with b+c>ell need not be computed. After the indicated column permutation the whole matrix is block lower triangular, with one diagonal G_j and ell−1 diagonals αG_j. Consequently
 det G_(j+1)=±α^((ell−1)N_j)(det G_j)^ell.
The block-size exponent is recorded correctly; only invertibility is needed. G_0=(τ(T_w T_v)) has entries q_H^length(w) δ_(v,w^-1), by the ordinary finite-Hecke basis multiplication. Thus its determinant is a unit. Induction makes detG_n a unit. Since B and C are actual R-bases, τ identifies H_n with its R-dual: it is a perfect symmetric associative pairing. No fraction-field rank is substituted for a unit determinant.

6. Presentation base change commutes with forming H_n, and its universal PBW basis is free, so both the trace coefficients and the inverse Gram matrix base-change to ANY commutative ring in which all parameters remain units. In particular this applies to the LM deformation DVR O=F[t,t^-1]_(t−1), q_Ht andQ_at^(na). For n=0 use H_0=R with τ(1)=1. For ell1 this is the ordinary finite-Hecke trace (C consists of finite T_v); the proof still holds. The separate ell0,n>0 quotient is0, with its zero perfect pairing, and has no nonzero content sector or Schur standards. No claimτ(1)=1 is made for that zero algebra.
